text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.74% today to $129.35, extending a 3.26% gain over the past two weeks. The move reflects strength in oil prices—US crude climbed to $96.16 per barrel, while Brent sits around $100—driven by supply concerns from geopolitical tensions. Iranian attacks on tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz and the ongoing Red Sea conflict are keeping markets on edge about potential disruptions to Middle East oil exports, supporting prices for a major oil producer like ConocoPhillips.

Refining conditions also favor the company: Goldman Sachs flagged that diesel prices will likely stay elevated through 2027 due to tight refinery capacity, which typically means wider profit margins on refined products for integrated energy companies. This combination of higher crude prices and robust refining economics has momentum behind the stock.
